subject: Pricing ask: tier breakpoints + flexible credit model
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@finretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@finretail.com>, payments@finretail.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 13:14:00 -0400
Subject: Intro + ratecard request for high-volume pricing

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the demo last week. FinRetail is ramping a new personalization pipeline that will drive a bursty profile-enrichment workload. We expect a steady-state of ~4B tokens/month in Q4 with bursts up to 12B in peak weeks.

Before we loop in procurement, can you send your standard hosted-API rate card and confirm:
- Discount breakpoints (how pricing changes at 1B / 5B / 10B / 50B tokens)
- Whether unused committed tokens can roll over or be converted to burst credits
- Overage pricing when we exceed committed tiers
- Any minimum commitment period (term) for deep discounts

Also, we may want a hybrid: a base commit with an extra pool of "flex credits" that buy burst capacity at a discounted overage rate. Can Redwood model that?

Appreciate a one-pager and expected timeline to get legal/finance review.

—Jordan
Jordan Meyers
Head of Data Platforms | FinRetail
jordan.meyers@finretail.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@finretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro + ratecard request for high-volume pricing

Jordan —

Great to hear — thanks for the clear numbers. I'm attaching our latest hosted API rate card and a short doc that outlines a flexible-credit construct we've piloted with two customers. [attachment: Redwood_RateCard_Q3_v2.pdf] [attachment: FlexCredit_Terms.docx]

High-level answers up front:
- Breakpoints we typically price at: 0-1B, 1B-5B, 5B-20B, 20B-100B. Discounts scale with committed spend; examples in the attached PDF.
- Flex credits: yes — we offer a prepaid credit pool that can be applied to bursts and bought at a middle-tier discount; unused credits can roll forward for one quarter or be applied to next-period consumption at a reduced conversion rate.
- Overage: charged on actual tokens at the next non-committed tier rate; we can alternatively put you on a short-term burst addendum with capped per-token overage.
- Term: deeper discounts generally require a 12-month minimum commit. We can discuss a 6-month pilot with a smaller commit and an accelerated review for Q4 scale.

Rishi (cc'd) — can you draft a sample breakpoint table and scenarios for FinRetail's 4B steady / 12B peak? Ben, please include a note on margin impact for flex credits and recommended conversion rates. I'll package these for Jordan and loop legal once they pick an option.

Next step: Jordan, would 10am PT on Thursday for a quick pricing modeling session work?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Intro + ratecard request for high-volume pricing — model scenarios

Team —

I built three scenarios based on Jordan's numbers. Summary (rounded):
1) Conservative (base commit 4B/mo): 4B committed tokens @ $0.0009/token = $3.6M/mo; overage @ $0.0012/token; flex credits sold at 12% discount vs on-demand.
2) Standard (commit to 8B/mo with flex pool): 8B @ $0.0008/token = $6.4M/mo; flex pool 6B credits at 15% discount; overage becomes $0.0010/token.
3) Aggressive (commit to 20B/mo): 20B @ $0.00065/token = $13M/mo; flex credits optional; deepest tier unlocked for model variants and priority routing.

Key negotiation levers: tier breakpoints, conversion window for unused credits (we propose 1 quarter rollover), minimum commit length, and whether flex credits are refundable (we typically don't refund, but will allow credit conversion to next quarter).

Ben — margin sensitivity attached in the spreadsheet (summary below). We should anticipate Jordan pushing for: 20% off at ~10B, and 30% at ~50B. If they ask for 30% at 10B, we should counter with 15% + flex credits + 12-month commit.

I will generate the Excel scenarios and redlines for a sample contract clause for flex credits.

-Rishi

From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@finretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@finretail.com>, payments@finretail.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro + ratecard request for high-volume pricing — model scenarios

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement:
- FinRetail preference is for a 6-month commit initially, with an evaluation and automatic renewal clause unless we give 30 days' notice. Can Redwood support a 6-month initial term for the Standard scenario (8B/mo)?
- For flex credits: we need at least one quarter of rollover and the ability to reassign unused credits between Product teams within our org (same umbrella account).
- If we commit to 8B/mo for 6 months, what is the earliest we can get a legal SOW and a DocuSign-ready contract? We want to close before Sep 1 to be ready for Q4.

Also, pricing ask: I quoted internal stakeholders asking whether you can do 18% off at the 8B level if we commit to 6 months and prepay 3 months up front. That buys our finance team time to cycle payments.

Appreciate a short response to those three bullets and a proposed timeline.

—Jordan

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@finretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro + ratecard request for high-volume pricing — model scenarios

Jordan —

Thanks for the specifics. Short answers:
1) Term: We can agree a 6-month initial term for the Standard scenario (8B/mo) with an automatic renewal by default; legal will include a 30-day opt-out notice.
2) Flex credits: We support one quarter rollover and credit reassignment across sub-accounts under the same enterprise account; we'll add the reassignment language to the flex-credit addendum.
3) Timeline & prepay pricing: If FinRetail prepays 3 months at signing, we can offer an 18% effective discount on the 8B/mo Standard scenario (finance sign-off required). Legal can prepare a DocuSign SOW within 3 business days after finance confirms prepay terms and billing details.

Action items I will take this afternoon:
- Rishi to produce the final pricing table and conversion math for the flex pool and overage rates (deliver by EOD).
- Ben to draft margin caveats and recommended caps on flex-credit resale.
- I'll issue a DocuSign SOW template and HubSpot deal update (link below).

If those work, I'll request legal to issue the SOW and the PowerForm link so you can sign.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
